title: What are the CPD requirements for Chartered Accountants ANZ members?
description: CA ANZ Regulation CR 7: 120 CPD hours a triennium for CAs, 90 verifiable, 6 ethics hours, on-the-job limits, six year records and audit partner rules.
shortAnswer: Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ) Regulation CR 7 requires Chartered Accountants and Affiliate members to complete 120 hours of continuing professional development (CPD) each triennium, of which 90 must be verifiable, with at least 20 hours in each year. For trienniums starting on or after July 1, 2024, at least six verifiable hours must be in professional ethics. Associate Chartered Accountants need 90 hours and Accounting Technicians 60. Records must be kept for six years.
keyTakeaways: CR 7, issued May 23, 2025, sets hours by designation: CA and Affiliate 120 (90 verifiable, 20 a year); ACA 90 (67 verifiable, 15 a year); AT 60 (45 verifiable, 10 a year).
CR 7.3(c) requires six verifiable ethics hours per triennium for trienniums commencing on or after July 1, 2024, up from two. Pro rata reductions do not reduce the ethics minimum.
Verifiable on-the-job training can make up no more than 50% of verifiable CPD and must be documented on CA ANZ's form and verified by another person.
Members keep CPD records for six years (CR 7.6). Certificate of Public Practice holders cannot use the full or pro rata exemptions.
Audit engagement partners for public interest entities and New Zealand licensed auditors must also meet Schedule 1, which adds a self-assessment and a learning plan.
jurisdiction: Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ members worldwide)
regulator: Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ), with the New Zealand Institute of Chartered Accountants (NZICA) for New Zealand licensed auditors
appliesTo: Chartered Accountants, Fellows, Associate Chartered Accountants and Accounting Technicians
Affiliate members and New Zealand Non Member Principals
Audit engagement partners for public interest entities and New Zealand licensed auditors (Schedule 1)
Members who are registered tax agents, BAS agents, company auditors, liquidators, SMSF auditors or financial services licensees

sections.heading: What does CA ANZ Regulation CR 7 require?

blocks.text: CR 7 Continuing Professional Development sets minimum hours per three-year triennium that vary by membership designation. The regulation, [published by CA ANZ](https://www.charteredaccountantsanz.com/learning-and-events/managing-your-cpd) and issued on May 23, 2025, says its purpose is to set minimum CPD requirements "to develop and maintain the professional competence necessary to provide high quality services to clients, employers, and other stakeholders, and to strengthen public trust in the accountancy profession."

blocks.text: CR 7 also reminds members that the hours are a floor. Compliance helps members show they meet the ethical requirement to maintain professional knowledge and skill under APES 110 Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants (or the NZICA Code of Ethics in New Zealand), but "a greater level of CPD than that required under this regulation may be necessary" depending on the member's role.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects CR 7 as issued on May 23, 2025 and CA ANZ's Managing your CPD guidance as at November 2026. Members who adopted CR 7.3(c) early, before their next triennium, apply the old and new requirements proportionally across that triennium.

sections.heading: When does a CA ANZ triennium start, and what changed for ethics?

blocks.text: CA ANZ trienniums run from July 1, not January 1. For most members the first triennium commences on July 1 of the financial year after admission; members admitted before July 1, 1994 started on July 1, 1994, and New Zealand residents admitted before July 1, 2012 started on July 1, 2012. CR 7's own example is a member admitted on November 16, 2017 whose trienniums run July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2021, then July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024, and so on.

The ethics minimum tripled for trienniums starting on or after July 1, 2024. CA ANZ explains that since July 1, 2021 members needed 2 verifiable ethics hours per triennium, and from trienniums starting July 1, 2024 they need at least 6. Any development that relates to the fundamental principles of the Code of Ethics can count, from any provider, provided verifiable evidence is kept.

The ethics minimum is protected from reductions. CR 7.5(c) states that pro rata exemptions "do not apply to the requirement for a Member to complete a minimum of six hours of Verifiable CPD in relation to professional ethics". A member on parental leave for most of a triennium still needs six verifiable ethics hours.

sections.heading: What counts as verifiable CPD and on-the-job training?

blocks.text: Verifiable CPD is learning supported by "evidence that is objective, and capable of being proven and retained in either written or electronic form". Non-verifiable CPD covers independent and informal learning such as technical reading, mentoring discussions and collegial meetings. For a CA, 30 of the 120 hours can be non-verifiable.

Verifiable on-the-job training is one-on-one training received while performing the role, or verifiable self-development, documented and verified by another person who need not be a member. CR 7.3(d) caps it at 50% of verifiable CPD. CA ANZ's commentary gives examples such as a new manager coached through a first review cycle, or a member learning forensic accounting under an engagement partner with 20 hours of documented learning. The training must be recorded on the CA ANZ On-the-Job CPD supporting evidence form.

items: **Facilitating or marking professional examinations** can provide up to 50% of verifiable hours per triennium (CR 7.9(c)(vi)).
**Participating in a NZICA, CA ANZ or CPA Australia quality review** is capped at 4 verifiable hours per triennium (CR 7.9(c)(vii)).
**Conferences, courses, committees, publishing and presenting** are listed as verifiable activities with no specific cap.

**Dual members** resident outside Australia and New Zealand, without a Certificate of Public Practice or specialization, can rely on compliance with a recognized body such as CPA Australia, the AICPA or ICAEW (CR 7.7).

sections.heading: Can CA ANZ CPD hours be reduced?

blocks.text: Yes, on a pro rata basis for most members, but not for Certificate of Public Practice holders or Affiliates. CR 7.5(a) excludes them from both the full and pro rata exemptions.

The minimums assume a 37.5 hour week over 12 months. A member can reduce hours pro rata for absence due to parental leave, unemployment or illness, or for part-time or casual work, and if the reduced total falls below 10 hours per triennium no minimum applies. A full exemption is available only to members who have permanently withdrawn from the workforce, including voluntary and pro bono work. The CA ANZ Board can also approve exceptional circumstances. A Certificate of Public Practice applicant who relied on exemptions or non-verifiable CPD has to establish competence another way.

sections.heading: What records must be kept and how is compliance checked?

blocks.text: CR 7.6 requires records of CPD activities and any exemptions to be retained for six years and provided to CA ANZ on request. Each record should include a description, dates, provider, relevance to the member's development, whether it is verifiable, a copy of the verifiable evidence, any link to a registration or specialization, the hours, and the basis for any exemption.

CA ANZ monitors compliance through annual notifications and reviews of a percentage of members' records, and reviews Certificate of Public Practice holders' records during practice quality reviews. Members who fail to comply may be excluded from membership under the By-Laws or NZICA Rules (CR 7.10). For a general method, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) and [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

sections.heading: What extra CPD applies to audit partners and registered tax agents?

blocks.text: Audit engagement partners for public interest entities and New Zealand licensed auditors must also meet Schedule 1 to CR 7. Within six months of each reporting period they must assess their competence against the learning outcomes in Appendix A, identify required CPD and build a prioritized learning plan of no more than three years, then update the assessment and plan at least once a year. Appendix A covers areas from audit and financial reporting to professional scepticism and independence threats. NZICA can vary, suspend or cancel a licensed auditor's license for non-compliance under the Auditor Regulation Act 2011.

CR 7.8 tells members holding Australian registrations, including registered company auditor, liquidator, trustee in bankruptcy, AFS licensee, SMSF auditor, BAS agent, tax (financial) adviser and tax agent, to ensure their training also meets those registrations. For tax agents, the [Tax Practitioners Board](https://www.tpb.gov.au/continuing-professional-education) accepts a recognized association's CPE where it is relevant and meets the TPB minimum, so one well-tagged CA ANZ record can serve both; see [TPB continuing professional education requirements](/regulations/tax-practitioners-board-cpe-requirements). A comparison with the other major Australian body is on the page about [CPA Australia CPD requirements](/regulations/cpa-australia-cpd-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can hold a Schedule 1 style competence map, with each learning outcome linked to planned and completed activities, which suits audit firms that must evidence self-assessment and learning plans. For other members it records whether each activity is verifiable, ethics related or on-the-job, so the 50% and six hour tests can be checked before the triennium closes. See the [professional services industry page](/industries/professional-services) for the wider approach.

faqs.q: How many ethics hours do CA ANZ members need?
faqs.a: For trienniums starting on or after July 1, 2024, at least six verifiable hours of professional ethics per triennium, within the total hours. Earlier trienniums from July 1, 2021 required two. The six hour minimum applies even when a pro rata exemption reduces total hours.

faqs.q: Can all CA ANZ CPD be on-the-job training?
faqs.a: No. Verifiable on-the-job training can make up no more than 50% of a member's verifiable CPD. It must reflect genuine development beyond business as usual, be documented on CA ANZ's supporting evidence form and be verified by another person such as a manager.

faqs.q: Do part-time CA ANZ members get reduced hours?
faqs.a: Most can reduce hours pro rata against a 37.5 hour week, and no minimum applies if the reduced total is under 10 hours a triennium. Certificate of Public Practice holders and Affiliates cannot use pro rata exemptions, and the six hour ethics minimum always applies.

faqs.q: How long must CA ANZ CPD records be kept?
faqs.a: Six years under CR 7.6, including records supporting any exemption claimed. Records should show the activity, dates, provider, relevance, whether it is verifiable with a copy of the evidence, any registration link and the hours claimed.
